name: check_closed
reason: C.closedErr ('I/O operation on closed file.', :51) is the first check of every C method model in source order (Share.write/getvalue/getbuffer too), and after the __buffer__ callbacks in C.writeItem (:242 before :246); the core simulation pins it against _pyio's closed checks, BytesIOWriteCallback pins that the check sees the state a __buffer__ left (C 'I/O operation on closed file.' vs _pyio 'write to closed file', probed on 3.15.2), and bytesIOTwinsAgree_refuted runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling.

name: check_exports
reason: bufferError carries the exact message (:61-62) and C.write/C.truncate/C.close/Share.write/Share.truncate test exports > 0 where :246, :696, :714 and :889 do; BytesIOGetbufferLive pins that every write (even b'', probed BufferError on 3.15.2), truncate and close raises it while a view lives, BytesIOWriteCallback that a view taken by __buffer__ triggers it, and bytesIOTwinsSameClassInRange_refuted runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-getbuffer-blocks-overwrite.

name: set_shared_buf
reason: platform applies: the body is only `self->buf_shared = 1` under Py_GIL_DISABLED (:87-89) and is empty on the default build.

name: clear_shared_buf
reason: platform applies: the body is only `self->buf_shared = 0` under Py_GIL_DISABLED (:95-97) and is empty on the default build.

name: resize_unshared_buffer_lock_held
reason: Share.resizeUnshared mirrors _PyBytes_ResizeKeepOnError (Objects/bytesobject.c:3418-3470: BadInternalCall at :3424, same size :3429, empty old :3436, newsize 0 :3446, copy when shared or hashed :3452-3468, else bytes_resize_inplace with the 33-byte OverflowError :3371-3374) keeping the object on failure; BytesIOWriteFailureKeeps and the by-value write pin state kept on failure, bytesIOTwinsSameClassNoExport_refuted runs the negative-size SystemError (bug pyio-bytesio-write-near-maxsize-systemerror), ZeroCopy pins getvalue's resize to string_size (value and identity), and HeldImmutable holds over it.

name: scan_eol_lock_held
reason: C.scanEol follows :133-152 (pos >= string_size gives 0, len clamped to maxlen when negative or too large, memchr for '\n' giving n - start + 1) and Share.readline runs it on the projected state; the core simulation pins it through readline/readlines/next against _pyio's byte-at-a-time IOBase.readline, and bytesIOReadlinesHintDoc_refuted runs it, bug pyio-readlines-hint-stops-early.

name: unshare_buffer_lock_held
reason: Share.unshare mirrors :159-175 with object identity: PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(NULL, size) (negative-size SystemError above PY_SSIZE_T_MAX, Objects/bytesobject.c:127-131; the empty singleton for 0, :137-139; allocation failure), string_size bytes copied, a fresh unhashed object installed as self->buf; HeldImmutable fails for an unshare that does not copy (the held object would change), ZeroCopy's shared branch and GetbufferLive's view contents fail for one that copies the wrong bytes, and the SystemError is run by the no-export refutation.

name: resize_buffer_lock_held
reason: Share.resizeBuffer/newAlloc mirror :181-229 in order: OverflowError 'new buffer size too large' above PY_SSIZE_T_MAX, the four allocation branches (the binary64 `size <= alloc * 1.125` is exactly 8*size <= 9*alloc for alloc < 2**47, checked), unshare when SHARED_BUF, else resize_unshared with alloc = 2**63 wrapped negative; the errors are pinned (no-export refutation, BytesIOWriteFailureKeeps) and the shared branch by HeldImmutable. The allocation sizes themselves are visible only through __sizeof__ and identity and are checked by the share difftest, not by a theorem.

name: write_bytes_lock_held
reason: C.writeItem runs PyObject_GetBuffer's __buffer__ (WItem.hooked: close, getbuffer, seek, write, or raise) before the checks at :246 and the pos read at :257, and Share.write mirrors the resize/unshare/in-place memset+memcpy path (:257-292) with identity; BytesIOWriteCallback pins the ordering (checks and position from the post-callback state, a raising __buffer__ propagating with its effects kept), writes-concat/getvalue-zero-fill/tell-after-write pin the copy and padding, HeldImmutable the unshare before an in-place write, and bytesIOHashConsistent_refuted runs the in-place path to the stale-hash defect (reproduced on 3.15.2: v == b'efgh', v not in {b'efgh'}; bug pyio-bytesio-stale-shared-hash, duplicate gh-160181).

name: bytesio_get_closed
reason: `.closed => s.closed` (Share: buf.isNone) with closed exactly when C clears buf (close, :890) and cleared by an __init__ with exact bytes (:1099); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.closed in every state, so an always-False getter fails after close.

name: _io_BytesIO_readable_impl
reason: C.xstep .readable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:326-327); BytesIOInquiries pins the exact ValueError on a closed stream, True on an open one, no state change and agreement with _pyio (_pyio.py:1022-1025), so neither an always-raising nor an always-True body passes.

name: _io_BytesIO_writable_impl
reason: C.xstep .writable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:341-342); BytesIOInquiries pins both branches, no state change and agreement with _pyio.py:1027-1030.

name: _io_BytesIO_seekable_impl
reason: C.xstep .seekable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:356-357); BytesIOInquiries pins both branches, no state change and agreement with _pyio.py:1032-1035.

name: _io_BytesIO_flush_impl
reason: C.xstep .flush is CHECK_CLOSED then None (:371-372); BytesIOInquiries pins the closed ValueError, None when open and no state change, against IOBase.flush (_pyio _checkClosed).

name: _io_BytesIO_getbuffer_impl
reason: Share.getbuffer is CHECK_CLOSED (:394) then the export of bytesiobuf_getbuffer_lock_held, with the view kept as (self->buf, string_size); BytesIOGetbufferLive pins one export added, read-through, write-through (view[i] = x shows in getvalue(), so a detached copy fails), IndexError past the end (message probed on 3.15.2), the BufferError refusals and release; BytesIOGetbuffer pins the closed ValueError against _pyio's.

name: _io_BytesIO_getvalue_impl
reason: Share.getvalue mirrors :416-432: a copy (or singleton) when string_size <= 1 or exported, else self->buf sized to string_size by an unshare (shared) or resize (unshared) and returned itself; BytesIOZeroCopy pins both branches by value and identity (a copy with no view, a zero-copy return under a view, or an unsized return each fail; `f.getvalue() is f.getvalue()` probed True without and False with a view), HeldImmutable holds over it, and bytesIOHashConsistent_refuted runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-stale-shared-hash.

name: _io_BytesIO_isatty_impl
reason: C.xstep .isatty is CHECK_CLOSED then False (:448-449); BytesIOInquiries pins the closed ValueError, False when open, no state change and agreement with IOBase.isatty.

name: _io_BytesIO_tell_impl
reason: C.step .tell is CHECK_CLOSED then pos (:463-464); the core simulation pins it against _pyio's tell after every operation sequence, including positions past the end.

name: read_bytes_lock_held
reason: Share.readBytes mirrors :476-493 in order (zero-copy when size > 1, pos == 0, size == PyBytes_GET_SIZE(buf) and no exports; the empty singleton for 0; else a copy) and C.readBytes the by-value slice; BytesIOZeroCopy pins the zero-copy return and its exports guard (fresh object with a view), HeldImmutable fails if the guard is dropped, and core/read-after-seek pin the sliced contents and pos += size.

name: _io_BytesIO_read_impl
reason: C.read and Share.read follow the clinic optSsize conversion then :514-524 (CHECK_CLOSED, n = string_size - pos, negative or too-large size clamped to max(n, 0)); the core simulation, read-after-seek (every p, n >= 0 including p past the end), bytesIOTwinsAgree_refuted, ZeroCopy's whole-buffer read and the __index__ models (read-index-twins refuted) pin it.

name: _io_BytesIO_read1_impl
reason: The body is `return _io_BytesIO_read_impl(self, size)` (:544) and C.step maps .read1 to C.read with the same converter; the core simulation runs read1 in arbitrary sequences against _pyio's read1 (= read), so a read1 with other behaviour fails it.

name: _io_BytesIO_readline_impl
reason: C.readline/Share.readline are optSsize, CHECK_CLOSED, scan_eol(size), read_bytes (:566-570); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.readline for every size, HeldImmutable covers its zero-copy return, and bytesIOTwinsSameClassNoAllocFail_refuted (readline(0) on a closed stream: C ValueError, _pyio b'') runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling.

name: _io_BytesIO_readlines_impl
reason: C.readlines follows :594-631: CHECK_CLOSED before the hint, PyLong_AsSsize_t for an int, -1 for None, the 'integer argument expected, got 'float'' TypeError (readlinesFloat), and a loop that breaks once maxsize > 0 and size >= maxsize; the core pins it against IOBase.readlines, and the hint-doc and float-twins refutations run it (bugs pyio-readlines-hint-stops-early, pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling).

name: _io_BytesIO_readinto_impl
reason: C.readinto and C.readintoSelf follow :657-675 (CHECK_CLOSED, len clamped to string_size - pos, 0 without moving when pos is past the end, memmove, pos += len); the core pins readinto into a foreign bytearray against BufferedIOBase._readinto, and BytesIOReadintoOverlap pins the overlapping copy into the stream's own view for every position, offset and length.

name: _io_BytesIO_truncate_impl
reason: C.truncate/C.truncateObj and Share.truncate follow :695-726: CHECK_CLOSED and CHECK_EXPORTS before conversion, PyLong_AsLong through __index__ (hooks that close, take a view, seek or write), 'negative size value', the re-checks at :713-714, string_size set before resize_buffer and restored on failure, pos untouched; BytesIOTruncateRecheck pins the re-entrancy guard, truncate-keeps-position/truncate-result the documented semantics, HeldImmutable the unshare of a shared shrink, core the twins, and truncate-index-twins is refuted (bug pyio-bytesio-truncate-index-deadlock).

name: bytesio_iternext_lock_held
reason: C.next is CHECK_CLOSED, scan_eol(-1), NULL without an exception (StopIteration) when 0, else read_bytes (:737-744); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.__next__ (StopIteration on an empty line) in every state.

name: bytesio_iternext
reason: The tp_iternext slot only wraps the lock-held body in a critical section (:751-753), a no-op on the default build; C.step .next is that body and the core pins it against IOBase.__next__.

name: _io_BytesIO_seek_impl
reason: C.seek mirrors :777-814 in order; BytesIOSeekSpec states the result against the mathematical sum for every in-range pos, whence and Py_ssize_t state (both 'new position too large' guards :789-793, :797-801, clamping, the closed/negative/bad-whence refusals in source order), so a wrapping seek fails it (probed on 3.15.2: seek(1, 1) at maxsize and seek(maxsize-1, 2) on 2 bytes raise, seek(maxsize-2, 2) returns maxsize); bytesIOSeekTwins_refuted runs the guard against _pyio, bug pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling.

name: _io_BytesIO_write_impl
reason: The body converts write_bytes_lock_held's count to an int or returns NULL (:832-833), which is C.write's `.ok (.int len)` / error; tell-after-write pins the returned count on every success, writes-concat makes successes non-vacuous, and BytesIOWriteCallback pins the callback path through it.

name: _io_BytesIO_writelines_impl
reason: C.writelinesIt mirrors :855-875: CHECK_CLOSED before PyObject_GetIter, the not-iterable TypeError, PyIter_Next whose __next__ may act on the stream and raise (KeyError ends the loop and propagates, :871-873), and write_bytes_lock_held per item returning at the first failure (:862-867); BytesIOWritelinesIter pins it as the next/write sequence for every fallible iterator in both twins, so swallowing the iterator's exception, continuing after a failed write or calling iter() before the closed check fails (probed on 3.15.2: KeyError after b'a' written, 'int' object is not iterable, closed ValueError first).

name: _io_BytesIO_close_impl
reason: C.step/Share.step .close mirror :889-891 (CHECK_EXPORTS, then clear, no CHECK_CLOSED); BytesIOGetbufferLive and BytesIOGetbuffer pin the BufferError under a live view (C refuses even an empty stream, probed on 3.15.2), the core pins close without one against _pyio, and the twins-agree and no-alloc-fail refutations run it.

name: bytesio_getstate
reason: C.getstateObj mirrors bytesio_getstate_lock_held (:909-935): getvalue's closed check, None for a NULL dict, else the dict's contents (PyDict_Copy, :925), the position; BytesIOPickleDict pins the dict branch through the round trip (a getstate that always returned None for the dict fails), BytesIOGetstate the closed refusals of both twins. Copy versus alias of the dict is not expressible (contents only); the state difftest checks it by mutating the returned dict.

name: bytesio_setstate_lock_held
reason: C.setstateObj mirrors :963-1022 in order over state objects: the 3-tuple TypeError (non-tuple or short), CHECK_EXPORTS, the reset, write of state[0] (non-buffer TypeError), PyLong_Check / PyLong_AsSsize_t / sign of the position (bool is an int), then None / dict merge (PyDict_Update) or install / non-dict TypeError; BytesIOSetstateChecks pins every refusal with the partial application left behind (probed on 3.15.2, all messages and resulting getvalue()/tell() match). The closed-stream path (write's ValueError after the reset) is modelled but not stated.

name: bytesio_setstate
reason: The wrapper only adds a critical section (:1029-1031), a no-op on the default build, around bytesio_setstate_lock_held, which BytesIOSetstateChecks and BytesIOPickleDict pin (see that row).

name: bytesio_new
reason: C.construct starts from ⟨[], 0, open, 0 exports, shared⟩, which is what :1059-1066 build (fields zeroed by tp_alloc, buf the immortal empty bytes), then runs __init__; BytesIOInitTwins pins that both constructors give bInit and that the twins then agree, so a tp_new that left the object closed fails the no-argument case; the NoMemory path cannot fire for the empty singleton.

name: _io_BytesIO___init___impl
reason: C.reinit/reinitObj/reinitItem mirror :1087-1110 (exports refusal first, reset of string_size and pos, exact bytes stored and the stream reopened, None skipped, otherwise write_impl then pos = 0); BytesIOReinitObj now pins the non-exact path (contents v, pos 0 and open on an open stream, so a missing `self->pos = 0` fails; the closed-file ValueError after the reset on a closed one; a __buffer__ running on the reset stream), with reinit and init-twins pinning the exact-bytes and int paths (probed on 3.15.2).

name: bytesio_sizeof_lock_held
reason: BytesIOSizeof quantifies over an arbitrary Share.St and restates Share.sizeof case by case (closed, shared, unshared; the proof is simp [sizeof] plus omega, and its 'covers the contents' conjunct is its own hypothesis), so it never connects __sizeof__ to a state a program reaches, leaving the allocation sizes newAlloc produces (the only non-constant part of the result) to the difftest; the 64 is tp_basicsize of the exact type hard-coded without a stated scope (a subclass with __slots__ = ('a', 'b') gives 80 + buffer, probed 117 after write(b'abc')).

name: bytesio_sizeof
reason: The wrapper only adds a critical section (:1137-1139) around bytesio_sizeof_lock_held, whose only theorem restates its definition (see that row).

name: bytesio_traverse
reason: no-behaviour applies by the GC policy: Py_VISIT of the type, dict and buf only.

name: bytesio_clear
reason: no-behaviour applies by the tp_clear policy: it only drops the dict and, with no exports, the buffer (:1157-1160).

name: bytesiobuf_getbuffer_lock_held
reason: Share.exportPrep/getbuffer mirror :1243-1252: the unshare of a shared buffer before the first export, PyBuffer_FillInfo as a writable view over (self->buf, string_size), exports + 1; HeldImmutable fails if the unshare is skipped (a view store would change a held bytes), GetbufferLive pins the export count, read- and write-through and the IndexError bound at string_size, and in-range is refuted with it, bug pyio-bytesio-getbuffer-blocks-overwrite.

name: bytesiobuf_getbuffer
reason: The slot adds the obsolete view == NULL BufferError (:1259-1263, unreachable from Python since PyMemoryView_FromObject always passes a view) and a no-op critical section around bytesiobuf_getbuffer_lock_held, which GetbufferLive and HeldImmutable pin (see that row).

name: bytesiobuf_releasebuffer
reason: bRelease and Share.release are exports - 1 (:1277); BytesIOReleaseExports and GetbufferLive pin that getbuffer then release restores the count, with contents and position unchanged, so a release that did nothing or reset the count to 0 fails.

name: bytesiobuf_traverse
reason: no-behaviour applies by the GC policy: Py_VISIT of the type and the source BytesIO only.

name: bytesiobuf_dealloc
reason: no-behaviour applies by the dealloc policy: it untracks, drops the source reference and frees, calling nothing itself.
